item.title: Trump says Houthis are "behaving very badly." What are his options?
item.description: Saudi Arabia said it intercepted Houthi missiles and drones across the kingdom on Tuesday after the rebel group struck an airport over the weekend. CBS News Middle East contributor Courtney Kealy joins with analysis.

item.title: Texts reveal communications between Jane Doe and male Cornell student after alleged gang rape
item.description: New text messages obtained by CBS News reveal communications between Cornell's Jane Doe and one of the men she later accused of assault in the alleged 2024 gang rape. CBS News crime reporter Anna Schecter breaks down the details.

item.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle ousted as ambassador over corruption allegations
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle said she is stepping aside as U.S. ambassador to Greece, days after reports that she offered access to officials in exchange for help paying off her debt.

item.title: Pope Leo recovering from surgery at hospital amid lung cancer diagnosis
item.description: Pope Leo has been diagnosed with lung cancer after surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican announced Tuesday. CBS News foreign correspondent Chris Livesay reports. Then, thoracic surgeon Dr. Kalvin Lung joins to discuss the diagnosis.

item.title: New details in text messages between Jane Doe and frat member
item.description: One of the accused fraternity members, who was later expelled, wrote to her: "I genuinely hope ur not catching as much heat from this as we r."

item.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer after undergoing surgery
item.description: Tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung cancer for Pope Leo XIV, the Vatican said in a medical update after he underwent surgery.

item.title: Six Flags closes 9 rides across 6 parks after deadly incident
item.description: Six Flags has temporarily closed rides similar to Goliath, the roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia that a man fell from.

item.title: Trump officials now leaning against execution livestream, sources say
item.description: Last week, the Pentagon had said the execution of the ex-Army major convicted of killing 13 in 2009 would be livestreamed.

item.title: OpenAI employee accused of planting recording device in office
item.description: A Saudi national who worked at OpenAI as an engineer is suspected of planting a recording device in one of the company's conference rooms.

item.title: New York City changes name of street containing Spider-Man's Queens home
item.description: For 37 years, a Queens house has been identified as the childhood home of Spider Man, aka, Peter Parker. The images and exact address were revealed in the pages of "The Amazing Spider Man" back in 1989. Now, the city is honoring that legacy with a street name change. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Anthropic warns certain AI models could soon spread and replicate themselves
item.description: Ina Fried, chief technology correspondent at Axios, joins "The Daily Report" to break down the latest news in AI.

item.title: Trial begins for former Massachusetts officer accused of killing pregnant woman
item.description: Testimony began in the trial of a former Massachusetts police officer accused of killing a woman he'd been sleeping with since she was a minor, after she allegedly told him she was pregnant with his child. Tom Hanson reports from Boston.

item.title: Over $500 million spent on ads during Texas Senate campaign, AdImpact data shows
item.description: Hundreds of millions have been spent on the Senate race in Texas as Ken Paxton and James Talarico battle it out with only weeks left before the midterms. CBS News' Kaia Hubbard reports.

item.title: OpenAI employee arrested for allegedly bugging conference room
item.description: U.S. federal agents have arrested an engineer at OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, after the man allegedly planted a listening device inside an executive conference room at headquarters. Jo Ling Kent reports.

item.title: Trump officials now leaning against livestreaming Fort Hood shooter's execution, sources say
item.description: Trump administration officials are now leaning against livestreaming the Fort Hood mass shooter's execution, sources say.

item.title: Trump distances himself from Kimberly Guilfoyle: "She wasn't a member of the family"
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle, the former fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., is now also the former U.S. ambassador to Greece. She resigned on Tuesday, amid allegations that she asked a major donor to pay off her six-figure personal credit card debt, in exchange for access to the Trump White House. Weijia Jiang has more details.

item.title: Selma Blair pleads not guilty following alleged mid-air assault on Delta flight
item.description: Actress Selma Blair is accused of attacking flight attendants on a plane, a police officer and a nurse on the ground and is now facing federal charges. She pled not guilty to two assault charges on Tuesday. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: More texts revealed between Jane Doe, accused in fraternity rape case
item.description: Cornell University shut down all fraternity house parties and social events for the rest of the school year as officials investigate allegations of a gang rape that occurred at a frat in 2024. Mark Strassmann has more.

item.title: Witnesses of Six Flags roller coaster death speak on incident
item.description: Six Flags announced that multiple thrill rides across the country will be shut down temporarily after a 42-year-old father died on Monday on a roller coaster in Georgia. Skyler Henry reports on the victim and what may have gone wrong.

item.title: Details on Pope Leo XIV's lung cancer diagnosis, surgery
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, the first American pope, has been diagnosed with lung cancer after surgeons removed the lower lobe of his right lung, according to the Vatican. Chris Livesay reports and Dr. David Jones, chief of thoracic surgery at the Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, has medical analysis.

item.title: Lung doctor explains Pope Leo's cancer diagnosis, operation
item.description: Pope Leo was diagnosed with of lung cancer following a surgical operation on Tuesday, the Vatican said. Dr. Charles Powell, chief of pulmonary, critical care & sleep medicine at Mount Sinai and director of the Mount Sinai Respiratory Institute, joins "The Daily Report" to explain what could happen next.

item.title: Fact-checking Trump's promises to lower prices
item.description: American consumers are facing higher costs for gas and groceries despite promises made by President Trump during his campaign in 2024. CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Trump travels to Alaska for rally amid tight Senate race between Sullivan and Peltola
item.description: President Trump is traveling 3,400 miles to Alaska on Tuesday to hold a rally amid a tight Senate race there between incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan and Democratic challenger Mary Peltola. CBS News' Anthony Salvanto and Weijia Jiang have more.

item.title: Pope Leo's brother also battling cancer, wife tells CBS News
item.description: Louis Prevost​, Pope Leo XIV's older brother who lives in Florida, has multiple myeloma, his wife told CBS News on Tuesday.

item.title: New Washington Post podcast tackles personal finance for "real people"
item.description: Personal finances are tricky, so the Washington Post launched a new podcast on Tuesday to help everyday people with just that. Michelle Singletary, host of "Dollars & Sense," joins "The Takeout" to discuss her approach to the show.

item.title: Democrats say Kamala Harris wasted 2026, Politico reports
item.description: Is former Vice President Kamala Harris setting herself up well for another White House bid? Almost two dozen Democratic operatives told Politico no. Political strategists Stephanie Valencia and Tiffany Smiley join "The Takeout" with analysis.

item.title: 10/13: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Vatican reveals Pope Leo XIV's lung cancer diagnosis after surgery; Kimberly Guilfoyle resigns as ambassador to Greece amid White House pressure.

item.title: Duane "Keffe D" Davis sentenced to 40 years to life for Tupac's murder
item.description: Duane "Keffe D" Davis​ was sentenced to 40 years to life in prison Tuesday in Las Vegas for the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur.

item.title: Anthropic warns "AI worms" could soon infect smart home devices
item.description: Small AI models could clone themselves and infect internet-connected devices such as smart TVs and appliances, the researchers warned.

item.title: California high-speed rail consultants billed taxpayers for late-night rides
item.description: CBS California Investigates obtained receipts behind the watchdog's findings of wasteful spending, revealing previously undisclosed connections to the high-speed rail CEO.
